### Primaquine regimens by G6PD status

| G6PD category | Radical-cure treatment policy | Treatment implementation | Follow-up approach | Follow-up implementation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **G6PD normal: > 70% enzyme activity** | TQ or high-dose 7-day PQ | Partially implemented | Conduct follow-up visits on days 0, 3, 7, and 28, then monthly for 3 months, and once at 6 months after completion of the radical treatment to monitor for relapses. | Implemented |
| **G6PD normal: no definition** | PQ 0.25 mg/kg/day over 14 days or PQ 0.5 mg/kg/day over 7 days if adherence is expected to be low and a risk-benefit analysis is conducted | Partially implemented | Conduct follow-up visits on days 0, 3, 7, and 28, then monthly for 3 months, and once at 6 months after completion of the radical treatment to monitor for relapses. | Implemented |
| **G6PD deficient: < 30% enzyme activity** | PQ 0.75 mg/kg/week weekly for 8 weeks | Partially implemented | Conduct follow-up visits on days 0, 3, 7, and 28, then monthly for 3 months, and once at 6 months after completion of the radical treatment to monitor for relapses. | Implemented |
| **If no testing available** | PQ 0.25 mg/kg/day over 14 days or PQ 0.5 mg/kg/day over 7 days if adherence is expected to be low and a risk-benefit analysis is conducted | Implemented | Conduct follow-up visits on days 0, 3, 7, and 28, then monthly for 3 months, and once at 6 months after completion of the radical treatment to monitor for relapses. | Implemented |

### Country-specific policy context

<div class="country-policy-context">Costa Rica has implemented tafenoquine, being the first country in Central America and the Carribbean implementing tafenoquine. Tafenoquine is the first choice for treatment of G6PD normal individuals. If not available use of PQ high dose If G6PD testing is not available, healthcare providers can refer the patient to a health facility that has testing as long as testing and treatment can be within 24hrs.</div>
